To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the prevalence of antibiotic resistance is higher among patients with cystic fibrosis than in the general population; 2) the use of antibiotics in patients with CF is associated with an increase in antibiotic resistance; 3) the prevalence of P. aeruginosa and S. aureus resistance is increasing; and 4) antibiotic resistance in CF is not associated with increased mortality.
the most important factor in the treatment of CF is early diagnosis and intervention.
antibiotic therapy for CF patients is complex and difficult, but that the results are generally good.

the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of antibiotics in Cystic fibrosis patients and the effects of antibiotics on lung function and sputum microbiology in these patients.

antibiotic use in CF patients is not well established.

there is no conclusive evidence that any antibiotic or any combination of antibiotics is superior to any other in CF.

there is a lack of evidence-based guidelines for antibiotic use in CF.
